note: Standard faces (docs/mechanical-interfaces.md). Motor-specific patterns live in catalog/interfaces.json; adapters convert between them.

AO-L.note: adapter on the motor output, CNC 6061-T6 from an instant-price service (D46): contact boss = the output flange, 0.6 mm relief elsewhere; sockets for the motor's pins; a Ø60 j6 journal (lengthened by print.journal_extra) for the 61812; the standard face with 8 x M5 tapped and 2 x Ø5 H7 dowel holes; the motor's 9 x M5 x 25 socket heads sit in pockets, below the face. made: 'print' gives the PA6-CF version (heat-set inserts)
AO-L.shoulder_note: the shoulder runs up to the bearing and seats only its inner ring (61812 inner-ring shoulder 62-64)

cnc.finish: as machined, deburred; no anodise (it would change the journal)

head.note: the motor's output screws: heads in Ø10 pockets, their tops 0.6 mm below the standard face (the link sits on the face; its spigot recess is only Ø40); 6 mm into the RS-04's 6.5 mm threads

AO-L.pattern_note: bolt_deg and dowel_deg are 15 deg from every RS-04 output screw (45, 75, 105, 165, 195, 225, 285, 315, 345): the old even pattern (22.5 + 45k) put six face holes 7.5 deg from a screw, where the screw-head counterbores broke into them, and both dowels on bolt holes (2026-10-27)

AC-L.note: printed motor plate: the motor lug pattern and spigot recess on one side; the 61812 pressed in from the motor side up against a 2 mm lip at the leg-side face (no retainers: the only axial load its outer ring sees is outward, from the adapter's shoulder lifting the inner ring, and the lip takes it; the face stays flat, 1 mm from the link); post and yoke-insert holes
AC-L.lip_note: the lip's bore at the leg-side face, over the bearing: clears the adapter's journal and the inner ring, bears only on the outer ring (61812 outer shoulder 72-76)

KC.pin: ISO 7379 shoulder screw, 12 mm shoulder, M10; length from the stack (a stocked length: the shin width takes up the rest)

PR.rod_end: M8 female rod end (igus KBRM-08 or SKF SIKAC 8 M)
PR.note: crank and shin lever parallel, at lever_beta_deg from the forward perpendicular (- = towards the foot): the rod's transmission sin = |cos(knee - beta)| stays >= 0.5 over the knee range (review A1); the rod is plain M8 threaded rod (buckling SF > 10 at the design load)
PR.rod: M8 threaded rod, class 8.8 steel, cut to length; two female M8 rod ends and jam nuts (length adjustable)
PR.pin: ISO 7379 shoulder screw, 8 mm shoulder, M6, head flush in a counterbore on the crank / lever outer face; washer + thin M6 nyloc on the thigh side

WH.note: PCD 64 so the M5 heads clear the BotWheel's Ø50 boss; the BotWheel's own M6 heads sit in pockets in the shin foot

CP.note: plain Ø18 pass through the printed walls (20 mm of PA6-CF): no grommet fits that thickness; break the edges

wheel_power.what: BotWheel phases (3 x 18 AWG) in a sleeve

leg_power.what: 2 x 14 AWG silicone, 60 V bus to the hip and knee actuators

print.note: D33: every made part is printed. Structural parts in PA6-CF (hardened nozzle; dry 8 h at 80 C before printing), 100 % solid where the CAD has walls; the rest in PETG. Bought hardware: bearings, steel pins and shoulder bolts, rod ends and threaded rod, screws, heat-set inserts.
